steps: Both of you go together to a Cook County Clerk Vital Records office (downtown: 118 N. Clark St., Room 120), with valid ID showing proof of age; you can start the application online first.
Sign the application and pay the $60 marriage license fee; the license is issued while you wait.
Wait 1 day: the license takes effect 1 day after it is issued and is valid for 60 days, for ceremonies in Chicago and suburban Cook County only.

Get married with your own officiant, or in person before a Cook County judge at the Marriage and Civil Union Court, 119 W. Randolph St. (lower level), Tuesday to Friday, no appointment; bring the license, ID and the $10 administrative fee.
Make sure the signed license is returned to the Clerk within 10 days after the ceremony; a certified copy of the certificate is $15.
left_out: Whether witnesses are required: not stated on the Clerk or Circuit Court pages read.
Opening hours of the Clerk's downtown Vital Records office: the locations page only says to click a location for hours.
Whether the Chicago courtroom takes cash only: only the Rolling Meadows and Bridgeview rows say cash only; the Chicago row does not say.
Any Clerk-run civil ceremony or ceremony fee: the Clerk's page sends couples to the Circuit Court's Marriage and Civil Union Court, so the $10 fee is quoted from the court's page.
Wait-time or capacity for guests at the downtown courtroom: not stated on the court page.

notes: WebSearch hit the tool's per-turn limit part-way through, so the florist and photographer lists are shorter than planned; nothing was searched around the limit. COURTHOUSE: the Clerk (cookcountyclerkil.gov) only issues the license; civil ceremonies are performed by a Cook County judge at the Circuit Court of Cook County's Marriage and Civil Union Court, so the $10 fee and the ceremony days/hours are quoted from cookcountycourtil.gov (cookcountycourt.org shows the same text). The Clerk's pages carry a banner: suburban offices closed on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3rd, and downtown offices run with limited staff. The Clerk's /service/marriage-licenses and /vital-records/marriage-civil-union/marriage-licenses URLs return the same page. VENUES: 9 listed; the cheapest are public or non-profit sites that print hourly or per-ceremony fees, not wedding packages. Oak Park permit and Berger Park are hourly rates, not packages. Berger Park's page lists room rates for special events and names weddings only for its outdoor ceremony permit, so check that a wedding is allowed in the Coach House. Garfield Park Conservatory: the $400 Jensen Room rate is the private rate for 4 hours, Mon-Thu; the page also prints a 2-hour 5-7pm whole-site slot 'great for a ceremony or proposal' at $1,500 with no guest cap stated. Cheney Mansion: 'Weekday: $2,900' sits under Weddings, Year-round; its guest cap and hours for that price are not on that page (the separate Petite Weddings page says up to 50 guests and prints no price). Astoria Banquets is in Buffalo Grove, about 30 miles out, so outside 'close suburbs'; the coordinator decides whether to keep it (it is the only commercial venue whose own page prints an elopement price with a guest limit). First Unitarian Church of Chicago (Hyde Park) prints 'The fee for a three-hour wedding block is $2,500 for the Sanctuary and $1,500 for Hull Chapel' (Hull Chapel seats 90) at firstuchicago.org/?p=446 and curl reads it fine, but that site stalls Python's urllib, so tools/verify_quotes.py cannot fetch it; left out for that reason only, add it back if the coordinator verifies with curl. Looked at and left out because the venue's own page prints no usable number or fails curl: Wicker Park Inn (small-wedding options listed, no price; its page code only shows a $125-$529 lodging range), Creativo Loft (website expired), Unity Temple, Pleasant Home (site did not load), Evanston History Center (no number on its own page), Guesthouse Hotel, 21c Chicago, Vice District Brewing (no price in the page HTML), Chicago History Museum (daytime rental $5,000, ceremony fee $500, no small-group package), Tiffany Celebration Garden (ceremony-only permit fee not printed), Chicago Public Library Winter Garden (wedding $7,000), Chicago Cultural Center (about $13,000+). Simply Eloped, Officiant on Demand ($2,199 to $5,399, 20 guests) and Tiny Wedding Co. ($4,775 to $4,990) are planners, not venues. Oak Park Conservatory's price is only in its PDF rental guide (the HTML pages send you to it); that server is slow (18 s alone, over 40 s when several downloads run together), so verify_quotes.py can flag it MISSING from a truncated download: re-run it alone. PHOTOGRAPHER: no own-site 1-hour courthouse package could be verified (Kristal Lee Photography's 1-hour $300 appears only on Zola; two Pixieset sites are blocked to curl). Adri Photo Co. mentions the courthouse by name, starts at two hours. Cheaper own-site alternative: Deandra Photography, 'Chicago Elopement Packages start at $950 and include up to two hours of coverage and the digital images' (deandaphotography.com/wedding-pricing); Becky Brown Photography lists a Chicago elopement package at $1,000 for a 2-hour session. FLORIST: Flowers for Dreams is Chicago-based; the $200.00 price is on the Lush / White & Cream self-service page and other style or palette pages may price the bouquet differently; the same page shows 'Petite Rose Bouquet Cream $55.00' as a cheaper small bouquet; its self-service weddings have a $200 minimum order. The price is rendered in the HTML (checked with curl).
